## Fresh Developments — Last 24-72h

**HIVE BUZZ HPC $220M GPU Contract (June 18 — freshest catalyst)**
HIVE Digital's BUZZ HPC subsidiary closed a 3-year, $220M sovereign AI GPU contract with Bell Canada and Cohere Inc., deploying NVIDIA GB200 NVL clusters. Goes live late 2026/early 2027; adds ~$70M contracted ARR atop current ~$35M (3x ARR inflection). HIVE simultaneously received council approval to acquire the Boden 32 MW data center (tenant→owner). Exactly the must-catch event flagged for HIVE: GPU/HPC contract win + ARR update.

**HBM4E Samples Shipped to Customers (June 19)**
Samsung and SK Hynix shipped 7th-generation HBM4E samples to major customers — ahead of the baseline timeline that had mass production no earlier than late 2026. Accelerates the supply-expansion side of the correction-risk thesis.

**MRVL +32% — Jensen Huang "Trillion-Dollar" Call (June 2, still in focus June 18)**
At COMPUTEX 2026 (June 2), Jensen Huang named Marvell the next potential trillion-dollar company, citing networking/connectivity as essential AI infrastructure. MRVL's largest-ever single-day gain. NVDA previously disclosed a $2B strategic investment in Marvell (March 2026). Jim Cramer reiterated the watch on June 18. MRVL market cap ~$250B vs $1T target.

**AMD +7.1% — MEXT Acquisition (June 15-16)**
AMD acquired MEXT, a startup whose AI-driven software makes NAND flash appear as DRAM to the OS, cutting memory costs 50% and expanding capacity 2-4x. Strategic fit with MI400/Helios 2H-2026 launch; closes a software gap in AMD's AI stack. Terms undisclosed.

**MU — Q3 Earnings June 24 (Pre-event)**
Street expects EPS $19.72 (+932% YoY) on ~$33.5B revenue. Prior Q2 beat by 38.6%. MU also gained +8%+ on June 15 (US-Iran peace deal, oil lower). High-conviction setup going into the print; TD Cowen target raised to $1,500.

**FSLR — Section 232 Ruling Imminent**
pv-tech.org reports Section 232 polysilicon tariff clarification could arrive by end of June 2026. FSLR hit an 18-year intraday high at $310.42 on tariff expectations; solar stocks +40% YTD. FSLR's CdTe thin-film technology insulates it from a silicon supply-chain tariff — positive binary catalyst this month.

**AVGO — Q3 Guidance $29.4B (+89% YoY)**
Broadcom guided Q3 2026 revenue ~$29.4B; AI semiconductor revenue alone ~$16B in Q3. Erste Group upgraded AVGO to Buy (June 5). AI revenue run-rate tracking above consensus.

**NVDA — $25B Bond Sale + Compute-Leasing Pivot**
NVIDIA completed a $25B bond issuance and is pivoting toward a compute-leasing model with multibillion-dollar commitments from major tech firms, extending revenue visibility beyond chip sales.

## Context vs Baseline

- **DRAM pricing**: Q2 +58-63% QoQ (NAND +70-75%) — memflation accelerating, DDR5 16GB spot at $201 (+42% M/M). Tracking above baseline.
- **HBM4E samples June 19**: Supply expansion is earlier than baseline assumed — keeps the post-2026 correction-risk signal valid and possibly moving the risk timeline forward.
- **Hyperscaler capex**: No guide-down. Aggregate $725B (MSFT $190B, GOOGL $190B, AMZN $200B, META $125-145B). META raised further on component-cost pressures. Top of baseline range.
- **Custom ASIC share-shift**: 44.6% ASIC shipment growth vs 16.1% for merchant GPUs (TrendForce) — materializing faster than baseline assumed; confirms the >1/3 compute thesis ahead of 2030.
- **Optical**: LITE sole 200G EML supplier at volume (1.6T pluggable). COHR ramping 6-inch InP across 3 fabs. InP lead times extend beyond 2027. CPO still limited-scale.

**Most Important Development**: HIVE BUZZ HPC $220M sovereign GPU contract (June 18) is the freshest must-catch — a 3x ARR inflection on NVIDIA GB200 deployment landing exactly in the AI/HPC pivot thesis flagged for HIVE. Close second: MU earnings June 24 is the single biggest near-term macro read for the memory/HBM thesis. MRVL's Jensen-endorsed +32% move from June 2 continues to reverberate (Cramer mention June 18).
